cases.rationale: A balanced reassociation passed P1 combinational equivalence, but the full ABC recipe produced the identical 102-cell/882-transistor estimate and the fast recipe slightly increased the transistor estimate (1044 to 1048). Synthesis already handles the expression, so the source rewrite is not recommended.

The shallower five-operand tree passed P1 equivalence, but mapped results disagreed: the full recipe regressed from 5262 to 5304 estimated transistors while the fast recipe improved from 7156 to 7040. The outcome is flow-dependent and does not support a recommendation.

Balancing only the independent sum output passed P1 equivalence. The full recipe regressed from 2626 to 2662 estimated transistors while the fast recipe improved from 3136 to 3102, so the small effect is flow-dependent and unfit for recommendation.

The procedural add-tree reassociation passed P1 equivalence, including bypass behavior. Full mapping regressed from 2118 to 2124 estimated transistors while fast mapping improved from 2628 to 2594; this recipe-sensitive result is not a proven improvement.

Factor the common addend as a + (sel ? b : c). P1 combinational equivalence passed. Both mapped recipes improved materially: full mapping fell from 184 cells/1536 estimated transistors to 93/840, and fast mapping fell from 213/1742 to 114/966.

The compact priority ladder directly specifies highest-bit-wins behavior and a distinct no-request valid result. Alternative casez or loop spellings offer no established PPA benefit and can alter unknown-state semantics; baseline elaboration and structural review found no candidate worth proving.

The 8-bit partial assignment is an intentional truncation boundary before the 9-bit result expression. Reassociating across that boundary changes carry behavior, so no arithmetic-tree rewrite is safe; baseline elaboration passed.

The signed balanced tree passed P1 bit-vector equivalence, but full mapping regressed from 1896 to 1932 estimated transistors while fast mapping improved from 2436 to 2402. Because the measured result reverses by recipe, the rewrite is not recommended.
The four-operand expression is already a balanced two-level add tree. Baseline elaboration passed, and no semantics-preserving structural improvement was identified.

Each sat_add call clamps before its result enters the next call, making the nested operation non-associative. Rebalancing would change functional behavior; the function boundary and saturation logic should remain intact.

This is the canonical one-entry elastic ready/valid register: readiness permits replacement on a consumed output, valid updates only when ready, and stalled data is held. Any control-path cut or extra storage changes latency or capacity and would require a different interface contract, so no P2 candidate is proposed.

The registered behavior deliberately combines the prior cycle's sum_q with the current cycle's c_i while valid_o follows valid_q. Moving c_i across a register or collapsing the stages changes the cycle relation or latency; no same-interface P2-safe improvement was identified.

The arbitration hotspot already uses masked requests plus a parallel-prefix leading-one primitive and reuses its prefix output for the next mask. Replacing it with a priority chain would degrade structure, and no local change preserves the hold/fairness state with a demonstrated benefit.

Depth-zero, singleton, and general FIFOs are already elaboration-time specializations, with pass-through, secure error, reset suppression, and occupancy behavior separated explicitly. No local state/control rewrite was found that preserves every parameter mode and justifies P2 candidate work.

The duplicated up/down counters, saturation enables, commit muxes, and invariant sum are security behavior rather than redundant logic. Sharing or removing the mirrored datapath would defeat the fault-detection contract; no P2-safe PPA candidate was identified.

Pack and unpack modes are constant-selected generate branches with direct shift, depth, and pointer logic. The apparent conditional chains encode clear/load/pull priority and ClearOnRead semantics; synthesis can prune inactive branches, and no proven structural gain was found.

The module is only a compatibility wrapper around spill_register_flushable with flush tied low. Elaboration removes wrapper wiring, while replacing the implementation would alter the established ready/valid and bypass contract; there is no local optimization candidate.

The implementation is already the minimal one-entry elastic register: ready is ready_i or empty, valid loads on readiness, and data loads only on a valid accepted transfer. No control or storage element can be removed without changing handshake behavior.

Pass-through, fall-through, simultaneous push/pop, non-power-of-two pointer wrap, flush, and memory write-enable behavior interact in the state update. The existing defaults and overrides encode those priorities compactly; no P2-safe local rewrite with a measurable rationale was found.

Request selection and payload multiplexing already use a logarithmic generated arbitration tree; fair mode computes the next request with two leading-zero counters, while unfair mode uses a small incrementer. A linear decode replacement would be inferior, and no P2-safe improvement was identified.

The module is already a canonical indexed data/valid mux with a one-hot ready decode. Re-expressing the indexed assignments as cases or loops gives synthesis-equivalent hardware without a demonstrated PPA benefit.

The parameterized skid, simple-buffer, and bypass modes are distinct protocol implementations selected at elaboration. The skid control's early-ready expression protects two-entry capacity under backpressure; no state/control simplification preserves all modes and sidebands with a proven gain.

This module is a structural cascade of configurable axis_register stages with direct endpoint wiring. Changing stage count or register type changes latency, capacity, or ready-path behavior and falls under the P3 transaction contract; no same-contract source optimization exists in the wrapper.

The design deliberately trades per-stage registered ready/valid paths for a decoupling output FIFO, including half-full throttling and sideband storage. Simplifying pointers, throttle state, or pipeline registers changes capacity or backpressure timing; no P2-safe local PPA candidate was established.
